en: prickly; irritable; (skin) dry and rough; haggard

examples.en: My younger brother is a bit prickly today.
My skin was dry and rough because I couldn't sleep.
He's a prickly person, so it's hard to talk to him.
Everyone will get irritable during exam period.
When my friend is hungry, he gets snippy and curt.
The team leader was sharp in the meeting, so I got nervous.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 '예민하고 말이 날카롭다'는 느낌이고, 피부나 수염에 쓰면 '거칠고 윤기가 없다'는 뜻이에요. 살이 빠져 수척해 보이는 얼굴에도 써요. '화나다'처럼 한순간의 감정이 아니라 계속되는 태도에 가까워요. '까칠남', '까칠녀'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: For people, 까칠하다 means sharp, touchy, and hard to please; for skin or stubble it means rough and lacking moisture. It can also describe a thin, worn-out face. Unlike 화나다, it is a lasting attitude rather than a momentary feeling. It also appears as 까칠남 and 까칠녀.

examples.en: I twist the towel to wring out the water.
Someone twisted my arm.
If you twist the bottle cap, it opens easily.
I stretched while twisting my body.
The child is squirming and saying no.
Don't twist your wrist too hard.

explain: '돌리다'는 한쪽 방향으로 돌리는 거고, '비틀다'는 양쪽에서 반대로 힘을 줘서 꼬는 느낌이에요. 그래서 수건, 팔, 몸처럼 꼬이는 것에 써요. 몸이 휘청거릴 때는 '비틀거리다'를 써요.
explain_en: 돌리다 turns something in one direction; 비틀다 applies force from opposite sides so the thing gets twisted. That is why it goes with towels, arms, and bodies. For a person who staggers, Korean uses a related word, 비틀거리다.

examples.en: I memorized all the words before the exam.
I memorize song lyrics quickly.

examples.ko: 전화번호를 암기하는 사람이 요즘 별로 없어요.
examples.en: Few people memorize phone numbers these days.

examples.ko: 이 문장을 암기하면 말하기가 쉬울 거예요.
examples.en: If you memorize this sentence, speaking will be easy.
Try to understand instead of just memorizing blindly.
I went having memorized my presentation, but I was still nervous.

explain: '외우다'가 일상에서 훨씬 많이 쓰는 말이고, '암기하다'는 시험 공부나 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 대화에서는 보통 '단어를 외워요'라고 해요. '암기 과목', '암기력'처럼 합쳐 쓰는 말이 많아요.
explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say 외우다 much more often; 암기하다 sounds stiffer and belongs to study and writing. You will hear 단어를 외워요 in conversation. It also appears in compounds like 암기 과목 (a subject learned by rote) and 암기력 (memory ability).

examples.en: I hurt my ankle ligament playing soccer.
My ligament was stretched, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 무릎 인대를 다치지 않게 운동 전에 준비운동을 해요.
examples.en: I warm up before exercise so I don't hurt my knee ligaments.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 인대 검사를 해 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said we should do a ligament test.
People with weak ligaments often sprain things.

examples.ko: 수술 뒤에 인대가 붙을 때까지 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: After surgery, you have to rest until the ligament heals.

explain: 뼈와 뼈를 이어 주는 질긴 조직이고, 발목이나 무릎을 다쳤다는 말에서 자주 들어요. '근육'은 움직이게 하는 부분, '인대'는 관절을 붙잡아 주는 부분이에요. 보통 '인대가 늘어나다', '인대가 끊어지다'로 써요.
explain_en: A ligament connects bone to bone, and you mostly hear the word when someone hurts an ankle or knee. 근육 (muscle) moves the body, while 인대 holds the joint in place. Typical verbs are 늘어나다 (stretch) and 끊어지다 (tear).

examples.en: I bought a new refrigerator before moving.
If you want to marry, you must get a home first.
My mother is preparing the holiday food.

examples.ko: 차를 장만하는 데 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: It costs a lot to get a car.
It's convenient to get winter clothes ahead of time.
I'll get a desk this month.

explain: '사다'는 그냥 물건을 사는 것이고, '장만하다'는 필요해서 미리 갖추는 느낌이에요. 집, 차, 가구처럼 크거나 꼭 필요한 것에 잘 써요. 명절 음식을 '준비하다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: 사다 simply means to buy; 장만하다 carries the feeling of getting something you need and having it ready. It fits big or essential things such as a house, a car, or furniture. It can also mean preparing food for a holiday.

examples.en: I saw a bull for the first time in a country village.
A bull is really strong.
My grandfather plowed the field with an ox.
That bull suddenly ran toward us and I was startled.

examples.ko: 황소만큼 큰 개를 키우는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone keeps a dog as big as an ox.

examples.ko: 동상 앞에 황소 두 마리가 서 있어요.
examples.en: Two bulls are standing in front of the statue.

explain: 그냥 '소'라고 하면 암컷과 수컷 모두예요. '황소'는 크고 힘센 수컷 소, 특히 농사일을 하던 소를 말해요. 암소는 '암소', 어린 소는 '송아지'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 황소고집이라서 한번 정하면 안 바꿔요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한번 마음먹으면 절대 안 바꾸는 아주 센 고집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes extreme stubbornness; someone who never changes their mind once it is made up.

explain_en: 소 on its own covers cows and bulls alike; 황소 is the big, powerful male, especially the kind used for farm work. A female is 암소 and a calf is 송아지.

examples.en: My grandmother put a charm in my bag.

examples.ko: 이 부적은 시험 잘 보라고 받은 거예요.
examples.en: I got this charm to do well on the exam.

examples.ko: 지갑 속 부적이 행운을 가져다줄 거예요.
examples.en: The charm in my wallet will bring luck.
I bought a charm at the temple.

examples.ko: 부적처럼 항상 그 반지를 끼고 다녀요.
examples.en: I always wear that ring like a lucky charm.

examples.ko: 차에 부적을 걸어 두는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hang a charm in their car.

explain: 원래는 종이에 글씨나 그림을 그려 몸에 지니는 물건이에요. 요즘은 '행운의 물건'이라는 뜻으로도 말해요. 같은 발음인 '부적당하다'의 '부적'과는 관계없어요.
explain_en: Traditionally it is paper with writing or a drawing that you carry on your body for luck or protection. People today also use it loosely for any lucky object. It has nothing to do with the 부적 inside 부적당하다 (unsuitable).

examples.en: This outfit is unsuitable for an interview.
It's an unsuitable movie for children.
That place was unsuitable for a gathering.
The weather is bad, so it's unsuitable and dangerous for hiking.
If you think it's inappropriate, please say so.

examples.ko: 이 재료는 요리에 부적당해서 쓰지 않아요.
examples.en: This ingredient is unsuitable for cooking, so we don't use it.

explain: '알맞다', '적당하다'의 반대쪽 말이에요. 말투가 딱딱해서 안내문, 심사, 서류에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '안 어울려요', '안 맞아요'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of 적당하다 (suitable). The tone is formal, so it shows up in notices, evaluations, and documents. In daily talk people more often say 안 어울려요 or 안 맞아요.

examples.en: I got a chest X-ray at the hospital.
There was no problem on the X-ray.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 엑스레이 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me the X-ray image.
At the dentist I had an X-ray taken and then got treatment.

examples.ko: 엑스레이가 나오려면 십 분쯤 기다려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to wait about ten minutes for the X-ray.
At the airport they check bags with an X-ray.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. 사진을 찍는 것처럼 '찍다'를 쓰는 게 특징이에요. 더 정확한 검사인 'CT'나 'MRI'와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: At the hospital you say 엑스레이를 찍다, using 찍다 (take a photo) with it. It often appears together with the more detailed scans CT and MRI.

examples.en: The new employees gathered at the training center.
This training center is in the mountains, so it's quiet.

examples.ko: 회사 연수원에서 일주일 동안 교육을 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a week of training at the company training center.

examples.ko: 연수원이 너무 멀어서 버스를 두 번 탔어요.
examples.en: The training center was so far that I took two buses.
Teachers go to a training center for training during vacation.
The food at the training center cafeteria was better than I expected.

explain: 회사나 학교, 기관이 직원이나 교사를 교육하려고 만든 곳이에요. 숙소와 강의실, 식당이 같이 있는 경우가 많아요. 학생이 다니는 '학원'과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is a facility an organization such as a company or a school system runs to train its staff. It often has rooms, classrooms, and a cafeteria in one place. It is different from a 학원, a private academy that students attend.

examples.en: That model's hair has a glossy shine.

examples.ko: 이 샴푸를 쓰면 윤기를 느낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this shampoo you can feel the gloss.

examples.ko: 갓 지은 밥은 윤기가 나서 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: Freshly cooked rice has a sheen and looks delicious.
My skin had no glow, so I put on cream.
Pick the fruit that has a shine.

examples.ko: 오래 쓴 가죽 가방은 윤기가 더 깊어져요.
examples.en: A well-used leather bag gets a deeper luster.

explain: 머리카락, 피부, 밥, 과일처럼 건강하고 맛있어 보이는 것의 반짝임을 말해요. 금속이나 유리의 '반짝임'과는 달리 부드럽고 촉촉한 느낌이에요. '윤기가 나다', '윤기가 흐르다'로 써요.
explain_en: It describes the healthy glow of hair, skin, rice, or fruit. Unlike the sparkle of metal or glass, it feels soft and moist. The usual verbs are 나다 and 흐르다, as in 윤기가 나다 and 윤기가 흐르다.

examples.ko: 이번 휴가는 최장 열흘까지 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take up to ten days off this time.
This tunnel is the longest in our country.

examples.ko: 비는 최장 사흘 동안 올 거예요.
examples.en: The rain will last three days at most.
Who set the longest record?
I heard the holiday can be as long as nine days.

examples.ko: 최장 거리를 걸은 사람에게 상을 줬어요.
examples.en: They gave a prize to the person who walked the farthest.

explain: '가장 긴'이라는 뜻이지만 '최장 열흘'처럼 숫자 앞에서 '길어야 이만큼'이라는 상한선을 말할 때 특히 많이 써요. 반대로 '가장 짧은'은 '최단'이에요. 시간, 거리, 기간에 쓰고 사람 키에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It means the longest, but it is most often placed before a number, as in 최장 열흘, to set an upper limit: at most ten days. The opposite is 최단 (the shortest). It is used for time, distance, and duration, not for a person's height.

examples.en: We discussed the new plan at the meeting.
In class, we discuss the topic in groups.
Everyone gathered, discussed ways, and decided.

examples.ko: 내일 토의할 내용을 미리 읽어 오세요.
examples.en: Please read tomorrow's discussion material beforehand.
If we discuss for long, good ideas come out.

examples.ko: 학생들이 쓰레기 문제를 토의하는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched students discussing the garbage problem.

explain: '토의하다'는 답을 같이 찾으려고 의견을 나누는 거고, '토론하다'는 찬성과 반대로 나뉘어 논쟁하는 느낌이에요. 일상에서는 '이야기하다'가 흔하고, '토의하다'는 회의나 수업에서 써요.
explain_en: 토의하다 is exchanging opinions to find an answer together, while 토론하다 means arguing from opposing sides, closer to debate. In daily life 이야기하다 is the common choice; 토의하다 is for meetings and classes.

en: gasp; gasping; whoa (sound of sudden shock)

examples.en: Gasp, I didn't bring my wallet!

examples.ko: 뒤에서 소리가 나서 헉 하고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A sound came from behind and I gasped in shock.
Whoa, it's already ten o'clock?

examples.ko: 계단을 뛰어 올라오느라 헉 숨이 찼어요.
examples.en: I ran up the stairs and was out of breath.
I gasped when I saw the price.

examples.ko: 친구가 헉 하는 소리를 내며 뒤로 물러섰어요.
examples.en: My friend made a gasping sound and stepped back.

explain: 갑자기 놀라거나 숨이 찰 때 나오는 소리예요. 문자나 메신저에서 '헉'이라고만 보내도 놀랐다는 뜻이 돼요. 비슷한 '헐'은 어이없거나 놀랄 때, '아'는 깨달았을 때 써서 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is the sound you make when startled or out of breath. In texts a bare 헉 means you are shocked. 헐 is similar but leans toward disbelief, and 아 is for sudden understanding, so the feelings differ.

examples.en: I usually go home at six.
I got home late yesterday and went straight to bed.
On my way home I stopped by the market.
It's raining, so please head home early.
I got word that the child got home safely.
After the company dinner, I'll go home by taxi.

explain: '집에 가다'와 뜻은 같지만 딱딱한 말이라 직장, 뉴스, 학교 안내에서 많이 나와요. 친구에게는 '집에 가'라고 해요. '귀가 시간'(집에 돌아오는 시간)처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as 집에 가다 but sounds formal, so you see it in workplaces, news, and school notices. To a friend you would say 집에 가. It also forms nouns like 귀가 시간 (time to be home).

examples.en: On Easter, churches hand out eggs.

examples.ko: 부활절은 해마다 날짜가 달라서 달력을 확인해요.
examples.en: Easter falls on a different date every year, so I check the calendar.
On Easter morning I attended a service with my family.
My friend decorated the Easter eggs beautifully.
After Easter the weather gets warm.

examples.ko: 해외에서는 부활절 연휴에 여행 가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Abroad, many people travel over the Easter holiday.

explain: 기독교에서 예수의 부활을 기념하는 날이에요. 한국에서는 공휴일이 아니라서 쉬는 날은 아니고 교회 행사로 지내요. 크리스마스와 달리 날짜가 해마다 바뀌고 항상 일요일이에요.
explain_en: It is the Christian day marking the resurrection of Jesus. In Korea it is not a public holiday, so it is observed mainly through church events. Unlike Christmas, the date changes every year and always falls on a Sunday.

examples.en: I took a trip to the west coast over the weekend.
The sunset seen from the west coast is really pretty.
On the west coast the tide comes in and out a lot.
The west coast highway was jammed, so I was late.
They say it will rain a lot on the west coast.
I dug for clams on the west coast mudflats.

explain: 한국에서는 서쪽 바다, 곧 황해를 따라 있는 바닷가를 말해요. 동해안과 달리 갯벌이 넓고 물이 빠졌다 들어오는 차이가 커요. 반대쪽은 '동해안', 남쪽은 '남해안'이에요.
explain_en: In Korea it refers to the coast along the western sea, the Yellow Sea. Unlike the east coast, it has wide mudflats and a big tidal range. The other coasts are 동해안 (east) and 남해안 (south).

examples.ko: 그 친구를 영영 못 볼까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried I may never see that friend again.
I never found the ring I lost.

examples.ko: 그는 고향을 떠나 영영 돌아오지 않았어요.
examples.en: He left his hometown and never came back.

examples.ko: 이러다가 영영 한국어를 못 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: At this rate, I feel I'll never speak Korean.

examples.ko: 영영 안 올 줄 알았는데 왔네요.
examples.en: I thought he'd never come, but he did.
That letter was never delivered.

explain: 거의 항상 '못', '안', '없다'처럼 부정하는 말과 같이 써서 '다시는 ~하지 않는다'는 느낌이에요. '영원히'는 좋은 뜻에도 쓰지만 '영영'은 아쉽고 슬픈 상황에 잘 써요. '영영 잊지 못하다'처럼 감정이 강할 때 써요.
explain_en: It nearly always pairs with a negative such as 못, 안, or 없다, giving the sense of never again. 영원히 can be used for happy things, but 영영 leans toward regret or sadness. It fits emotional lines like 영영 잊지 못하다 (can never forget).

examples.ko: 버스 정류장 전광판에 도착 시간이 나와요.
examples.en: The arrival time shows on the board at the bus stop.

examples.ko: 경기장 전광판을 보면 점수를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the score on the stadium board.

examples.ko: 전광판이 고장 나서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: The display broke, so nothing is shown.

examples.ko: 길 건너 전광판에서 광고가 계속 나와요.
examples.en: Ads keep playing on the electronic board across the street.
I checked the subway display before boarding.

examples.ko: 전광판 글자가 너무 작아서 안 보였어요.
examples.en: The letters on the display were too small to see.

explain: 전구나 화면으로 글자와 숫자를 보여 주는 큰 판이에요. 정류장, 경기장, 도로에서 볼 수 있어요. 종이로 된 '게시판'이나 '간판'과는 달리 내용이 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is a large board that shows letters and numbers with lights or a screen, seen at bus stops, stadiums, and roads. Unlike a 게시판 (notice board) or 간판 (shop sign), what it displays changes.

examples.en: He is released from prison this month.

examples.ko: 오 년 만에 출소한 남자가 인터뷰를 했어요.
examples.en: A man released after five years gave an interview.
He says he wants to live with his family once he's released.
It's hard to find a job after being released.
The news said he's due to be released tomorrow.
My brother was released, so the family went to meet him.

explain: 교도소에서 형을 마치고 나오는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '수감되다'예요. 주로 뉴스에서 많이 나오는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It means leaving prison after serving a sentence; the opposite is 수감되다 (be imprisoned). You mostly hear it in the news, and people are careful about using it in casual talk.

en: commute to school; go to school regularly

examples.en: I commute to school by subway.
My home was far, so I commuted an hour each way.
Many students bike to school.

examples.ko: 기숙사에 살지 않고 집에서 통학할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll commute from home instead of living in the dorm.
I memorized English words while commuting to school.
It's tiring commuting to school every morning.

explain: 집에서 학교까지 오가는 것을 말해요. 직장은 '출근하다', 학교는 '통학하다'로 나눠 써요. '통학 버스', '통학 시간'처럼 합쳐서도 써요.
explain_en: It means going back and forth between home and school. Korean separates 출근하다 for work from 통학하다 for school. It appears in compounds like 통학 버스 (school bus) and 통학 시간 (commute time to school).

en: filial devotion; devotion to one's parents

examples.en: That son is deeply devoted to his parents.
A devoted daughter takes care of her parents.
Grandmother was moved by her grandson's devotion.
He is known for his devotion to his parents.

examples.ko: 효성은 말이 아니라 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Filial devotion should be shown by actions, not words.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에는 효성이 큰 아이가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Old tales often feature a child with great filial devotion.

explain: '효도'가 부모님께 하는 행동이라면 '효성'은 부모를 위하는 마음이에요. '효성이 지극하다', '효성이 깊다'처럼 마음의 크기를 말할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 옛날 같아서 요즘은 '효도'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: If 효도 is what you do for your parents, 효성 is the heart behind it. It is used to describe how strong that feeling is, as in 효성이 지극하다 or 효성이 깊다. It sounds a little old-fashioned, so people today use 효도 more.

examples.en: At Lunar New Year I go down to my hometown.
My grandmother still celebrates the Lunar New Year.
The highway is jammed during the Lunar New Year holiday.

examples.ko: 구정은 해마다 일월 말이나 이월에 있어요.
examples.en: Lunar New Year falls in late January or February each year.
When Lunar New Year comes, we eat tteokguk.
I got New Year's money at Lunar New Year.

explain: 음력 1월 1일을 부르던 옛 이름이에요. 지금은 공식 이름이 '설날'이고, 양력 1월 1일은 '신정'이에요. 어른들은 아직 '구정'이라고 많이 부르지만 젊은 사람들은 '설'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the old name for the first day of the lunar calendar. The official name now is 설날, and January 1 on the regular calendar is 신정. Older people still often say 구정, while younger people say 설.

examples.en: A lizard is clinging to the wall.
My younger brother wants to keep a lizard.
A lizard cuts off its tail when in danger.
I saw a big lizard at the zoo.
It ran away fast like a lizard.
The lizard basking in the sun was cute.

explain: '뱀'과 이름이 비슷하지만 다리가 있고 꼬리가 끊어졌다가 다시 자라요. 그래서 '도마뱀 꼬리 자르기'는 윗사람이 책임을 아랫사람에게 넘길 때 비유로 써요. '도롱뇽'과는 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 윗사람이 책임을 피하려고 도마뱀 꼬리 자르기를 했다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: cutting off the lizard's tail (sacrificing a subordinate)
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생겼을 때 윗사람이 아랫사람만 책임지게 하고 빠져나갈 때 비유로 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for a superior sacrificing a subordinate to escape blame when something goes wrong. Often heard in the news.
phrases.en_equiv: make a scapegoat of a subordinate

explain_en: The name looks like 뱀 (snake), but a 도마뱀 has legs and can regrow a tail that it sheds. The saying 도마뱀 꼬리 자르기 (cutting off the lizard's tail) is used when someone in charge pushes blame onto someone lower. It is a different animal from 도롱뇽 (salamander).

examples.en: The child has cough and fever symptoms.
They check for fever at the entrance.
If the fever continues, go to the hospital.
Even after taking medicine, the fever won't go down.
The battery shut off because of overheating.
Patients with a fever, please wait separately.

explain: 몸이나 기계에서 열이 나는 것을 말하는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 사람이 아플 때는 '열이 나요'라고 하고, 병원이나 안내문에서 '발열'을 써요. 기계에는 '과열'(너무 뜨거워짐)을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for giving off heat, from a body or from a machine. In daily speech you say 열이 나요 when you are sick; 발열 appears in hospitals and notices. For machines that get too hot, 과열 is the common word.

examples.en: My grandfather has trouble walking.

examples.ko: 이 길은 보행 전용이라서 차가 못 들어와요.
examples.en: This road is for pedestrians only, so cars can't enter.
Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.

examples.ko: 무릎을 다쳐서 보행 연습을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I hurt my knee, so I'm practicing walking.
Pedestrians must follow the signal.
Wait until the walk signal changes.

explain: '걷기'와 비슷하지만 안내문, 교통, 의료처럼 딱딱한 자리에서 써요. '보행자'(걷는 사람), '보행 신호'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요. 운동으로 걷는 건 '걷기'나 '산책'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is close to 걷기 but belongs in formal settings such as signage, traffic, and medicine. It shows up in 보행자 (pedestrian) and 보행 신호 (walk signal). Walking for exercise is called 걷기 or 산책.

examples.en: Lemon tea has a fresh, zesty taste.
The morning air is fresh, so I feel good.
I bought soap that has a fresh scent.
The outfit you're wearing today looks so fresh.

examples.ko: 느끼한 음식 뒤에는 상큼한 과일을 먹어요.
examples.en: After greasy food, I eat fresh, zesty fruit.
That child's smile is bright and cute.

explain: 신맛이 살짝 나는 과일, 향, 공기, 옷차림처럼 기분 좋게 산뜻한 것에 써요. '신선하다'는 오래되지 않았다는 뜻이고, '상큼하다'는 맛이나 느낌이 가볍고 깨끗하다는 뜻이에요. 특히 귤, 레몬, 딸기 같은 맛에 잘 써요.
explain_en: It fits pleasantly light things such as slightly tart fruit, scents, air, and outfits. 신선하다 says something is not stale, whereas 상큼하다 describes a light, clean taste or feeling. It is especially common for citrus and strawberries.

examples.en: Yesterday I sent my parents some money.
You can send money easily with the app.
I send money right after I get paid.
There's a fee to send money overseas.
If you give me your account number, I'll send the money right away.
I sent money to the wrong person by mistake.

explain: 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '이체하다'도 쓰는데, '이체'는 은행 서비스 이름처럼 자주 보이고 '송금'은 상대에게 보낸다는 느낌이 강해요. 현금을 직접 주는 건 '주다', 택배로 보내는 건 '부치다'예요.
explain_en: It means sending money from your bank account to someone else's. 이체하다 is a close synonym that you see more in banking menus, while 송금하다 stresses sending to a person. Handing over cash is 주다, and mailing something is 부치다.

examples.en: The ceremony starts at twelve.
I went to my friend's wedding ceremony.

examples.ko: 예식 때 주차장이 가득 차서 오래 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The parking lot was full during the ceremony, so I waited a long time.
We had a small ceremony with family only.

examples.ko: 예식이 끝나고 다 같이 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After the ceremony, we all ate together.
We set the ceremony date for autumn.

explain: 주로 결혼식을 가리키지만 원래는 정해진 격식을 갖춘 행사 전체를 말해요. 일상에서는 '결혼식'이라고 하고, '예식'은 '예식장'(결혼식장)처럼 합쳐서 많이 써요. 장례는 '장례식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It most often points to a wedding but originally covers any formal event done by set protocol. In daily speech people say 결혼식; 예식 is common in compounds like 예식장 (wedding hall). A funeral is called 장례식.

examples.en: The heir's name is written in the will.
The eldest son is the only heir.
Heirs have to pay taxes.
The lawyer gathered the heirs and explained.
If there are several heirs, they split it.
You must decide on the heir who will receive the property.

explain: 돌아가신 분의 재산을 물려받는 사람이에요. 주는 사람은 '피상속인'이라고 해요. 뉴스, 법률, 은행에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '유산을 받을 사람'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the person who receives the property of someone who has died. The giver is called 피상속인. It is news, legal, and banking language, so in casual talk people spell it out as 유산을 받을 사람.
